questions.q: A rise in blood glucose enters pancreatic beta cells and is metabolised. Which event links this metabolism to insulin granule exocytosis?
options: Opening of ATP-sensitive K+ channels and membrane hyperpolarisation
Closure of ATP-sensitive K+ channels, membrane depolarisation and opening of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels
Inhibition of Ca2+ entry and reduced intracellular calcium
Activation of alpha-cell glucagon receptors on beta cells
questions.explain: Glucose metabolism raises the ATP/ADP ratio in beta cells. ATP-sensitive K+ channels close, depolarising the membrane; voltage-gated Ca2+ channels then open and Ca2+ entry triggers insulin granule exocytosis.

questions.q: During an overnight fast, plasma glucose is maintained partly by glucagon. Which hepatic process is stimulated early by this hormone?
options: Conversion of glucose to fatty acids
questions.explain: Glucagon acts on hepatocytes through cAMP-dependent signalling to stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis while inhibiting glycogen synthesis. Glycogenolysis is an important early source of glucose during fasting.

questions.q: A rise in blood glucose stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells. Which event directly triggers voltage-gated calcium-channel opening?
options: Closure of ATP-sensitive potassium channels and membrane depolarisation
Opening of ATP-sensitive potassium channels and hyperpolarisation
Inhibition of glucose metabolism and reduced ATP production
Activation of chloride secretion into the islets
questions.explain: Glucose metabolism raises the ATP/ADP ratio, closing ATP-sensitive K+ channels. Reduced K+ efflux depolarises the beta-cell membrane, opening voltage-gated Ca2+ channels and promoting insulin exocytosis.

open.q: What sequence links increased beta-cell glucose metabolism to insulin exocytosis?
accept: ATP rises, KATP channels close, the membrane depolarises, Ca2+ channels open and insulin is released

questions.q: A fasting patient has increased hepatic glucose output. Which intracellular second messenger is primarily increased when glucagon binds its hepatocyte receptor?
questions.explain: The hepatic glucagon receptor is Gs-coupled. Activation stimulates adenylyl cyclase, raises cAMP and activates protein kinase A, promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
